The main objections raised are as under: 7. The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 19.2.2026, in reply to the objections raised by the filed Sh. Rakesh Arvindbhai Patel & others have submitted as under: - c) The Co-Petitioner, KHTL, has complied with all applicable provisions of the CERC Regulations while filing the Petition, including publication of the public notice strictly in the prescribed format under the CERC (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Transmission Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2024. Accordingly, the objections filed by Sh. Rakesh Arvind bhai Patel & others may be dismissed and the petition may be considered on merits in accordance with law, without prejudice to the rights of the Applicant/ Transmission Licensee under the Electricity Act, TSA, and other applicable laws. 9. Vide RoP dated 24.2.2026, the Petitioner was directed to submit the amended memo of parties along with proof of service to the newly impleaded Respondents with a supporting affidavit within a week. In compliance with the same, the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 2.3.2026 filed the amended memo of parties along with proof of service to the newly impleaded Respondents. informing the parties, and granted two weeks’ time to the co-Petitioner (KPS III HVDC Transmission Limited) to serve notice upon the respondents, who may file their response within a week thereafter, and subject to the above, the Commission reserved the order in the matters. 12. We have considered the objections filed by Sh. Rakesh Arvindbhai Patel & others, and the response filed by the Petitioner. The objectors have, inter alia, contended that the public notice dated 18.12.2025 is vague and legally defective on the ground that it does not specify the exact route alignment, the names of villages, and the revenue survey numbers, and that detailed route maps were not made available for public inspection. It has also been urged that in the absence of such details, affected persons are unable to effectively raise objections, and therefore, a fresh notice ought to be issued. _Per contra_ , the Petitioner has submitted that the public notice dated 18.12.2025 was issued strictly in accordance with the requirements of the 2024 Transmission Licence Regulations. It has been further submitted that issues relating to route alignment, survey numbers, and land particulars fall within the scope of powers exercised under Section 164 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and are not germane to the present proceedings for the grant of a transmission licence. The Petitioner has also submitted that a subsequent public notice dated 12.2.2026 was issued inviting stakeholder comments in respect of such aspects, i.e., approval under Section 164 of the Act. 14. On the other hand, the objections raised by the objectors regarding specific route alignment, survey numbers, and land particulars fall within the distinct purview of Section 164 of the Electricity Act, 2003, which governs the procedure for conducting surveys and addressing grievances related to land use. The Petitioner has duly initiated the process under Section 164 by issuing a separate public notice dated 12.2.2026, specifically inviting comments on the route alignment and land particulars. The judgment relied upon by the objectors i.e., ( _Punjab State Power Corporation Ltd. vs. Ranjit Singh_ ) pertained to the validity of notifications issued under specific landrelated statutes where the primary intent was to inform affected landowners for acquisition purposes. The said judgment is distinguishable in the present context, where the notice is issued under the specific mandate of the Commission for granting a transmission licence. 16. The bidders holding the first fifty per cent of the ranks (with any fraction rounded off to a higher integer) or four Bidders, whichever is higher, shall be considered to be qualified for participating in the electronic reverse auction stage and submitting their final offer. - g) Completion of various activities as stipulated in the Final RFP including in particular Clause 2.15.2, Clause 2.15.3 and Clause 2.15.4 of the Final RFP, within the timelines as prescribed therein. However, as per the Petitioner, objections pertain to the grant of Section 164 approval not against the public notice published by the Petitioner in accordance with the provisions of the 2024 Transmission Licence Regulations. The Petitioner has submitted that it responded to the objections raised by certain stakeholders and also invited comments from stakeholders through a Public Notice published on 12.2.2026 regarding route alignment, village names, and land particulars of the proposed transmission lines.
